attrs.Hint: the Mountains of Aman, highest of the world: a curved wall near the east coast from north to south, pierced only by the Calacirya
Oiolossë, Mount Everwhite: highest mountain of the world, on the borders of the sea; Ilmarin on its summit. South of the pass after the HoME maps
highest mountain of the southern Pelóri, above Avathar; Melkor and Ungoliant climbed it to look on Valinor
the green hill raised in the Calacirya; Tirion stands on its crown
Corollairë, the green mound before the western gate of Valmar where the Two Trees grew
approx: the lake in the gardens of Lórien; Estë sleeps by day on the tree-grown isle in it
approx: Varda's great vats of the dew of Telperion and the light of Laurelin, near the Trees; Ungoliant drank them
the forests of the Huntsman in the south of Valinor, at the feet of Hyarmentir
approx: the gardens of Irmo, fairest place in the world, with the lake Lórellin; placed south of Valmar
Valimar of many bells, city of the Valar in the midst of the plain of Valinor
white city of the Vanyar and Noldor on the crown of Túna in the Calacirya
the tower of Ingwë in Tirion, whose lamp shone far out to sea
the Haven of the Swans, city of the Teleri on the coast of Eldamar north of the Calacirya
haven of the Eldar on the east side of Tol Eressëa, facing the sea; of the Second Age (Akallabêth)
Fëanor's stronghold and treasury in the hills in the north of Valinor; Finwë was slain at its doors
the halls of Manwë and Varda on the summit of Taniquetil
approx: the Halls of Awaiting in the west of Valinor by the shore of the Outer Sea
approx: halls west of West upon the borders of the world, near the Halls of Mandos
approx: the halls of the Smith of the Valar in Valinor; the text gives no place

approx: the door in the Walls of the Night beyond Ekkaia; the Ambarkanta (HoME IV) puts it in the far west, beyond the edge of this sheet; Morgoth was thrust through it into the Void after the War of Wrath (Silmarillion ch. 24)
the golden gates of Valmar on its west side, facing Ezellohar and the Ring of Doom
the Ring of Doom, where the Valar sat in council, near the golden gates of Valmar
the Pass of Light, the one cleft through the Pelóri, made for the Eldar; the light of the Trees flowed out through it
the Lonely Isle, ferry of the Eldar, rooted by Ulmo in the Bay of Eldamar
chain of isles set from north to south in the Shadowy Seas at the Hiding of Valinor (after the Flight of the Noldor)
the great bay of Elvenhome east of the Calacirya, with Tol Eressëa in it
the Outer Sea that surrounds the world, west of Valinor
the Great Sea between Aman and Middle-earth; the Sundering Seas
approx: where Ar-Pharazôn and his warriors lie under the hills that fell on them about Túna (Second Age, Akallabêth)
